newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Palesintians want UN Council meeting on peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Palesintians want UN Council meeting on peace crisis.

text.p: Palestinians leaders on Monday called on the United Nations Security Council to protest Israeli actions on the West Bank and Gaza, touched off off by a twin suicide bombing last week.

Nassir al-Kidwa, the Palestinian observer at the United Nations, said he had asked Council President Sir John Weston of Britain for a statement telling Israel to lift what he called aggressive measures against the Palestinians.
Kidwa, who also saw U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, said Weston would discuss his request with members on Tuesday.

The bombings in Jerusalem last Wednesday killed 15 people including the two Arab attackers, and plunged Palestinain leader Yasser Arafat's relations with Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to an all-time low.

Israel has suspended peace talks and sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, disrupting Palestinian trade and preventing tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state. It also threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to fight militants if Arafat did not clamp down on Islamic militants.
"We say that the Israeli government is committing an act of aggression against the Palestinian people and against the Palestinian authority," Kidwa told reporters.
"These actions represent an unprecedented form of collective punishment and they do not serve, and indeed run contrary to, the purpose of fighting violence and extremism."

"They are politically motivated. We are increasingly convinced that the current government is taking those actions to preempt any progress in the peace process and maybe to kill the process as a whole," he said.
Israeli actions, he said, were causing "all forms of suffering to the Palestinian people, including shortages of food and medical supplies and total economic destruction."

The moves by Kidwa at the United Nations were part of a diplomatic effort in the Middle East to find a way out of the crisis. Arafat was in Amman for late-night talks with Jordan's King Hussein. Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy was due to meet Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Tuesday.

The perpetrators of the latest suicide attacks are not known. A leaflet issued in the name of the Islamist Hamas group claimed responsibility but Israeli and PLO officials have questioned its authenticity.
